questions.q: What real trade-off does a one-week on-call rotation make compared to a shorter three-to-four day rotation?
options: There is no trade-off; rotation length has no effect on outcomes
A week-long rotation eliminates the need for a secondary on-call engineer
A bad week compounds for longer before the engineer gets a break, in exchange for fewer handoffs and less scheduling overhead
A week-long rotation is only valid for services with zero expected page volume
questions.explain: One week is easier to schedule but lets a bad stretch of pages compound longer before relief; a shorter rotation caps that exposure at the cost of more frequent handoffs.

questions.q: What does genuine follow-the-sun on-call coverage actually require?
options: Roughly three regions spread about eight hours apart, so one region is always in its daytime
A single large on-call team working from one office with flexible hours
Nothing beyond two offices in neighboring time zones
A paging tool that automatically translates alert times into local time
questions.explain: Full day-time coverage with no overnight gap typically needs roughly three regions about eight hours apart; two offices a few hours apart still leave an overnight gap neither side covers.

questions.q: What is the actual job of a secondary on-call engineer?
options: To be paged automatically if the primary doesn't acknowledge within a defined window, and to absorb concurrent incidents
To review the primary's postmortems after the rotation ends
To replace the primary permanently once the rotation starts
To only work on the days the primary is on vacation
questions.explain: An escalation policy with a timeout pages the secondary if the primary doesn't acknowledge in time, and the secondary also handles a second concurrent incident so the primary isn't juggling both alone.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat on-call compensation as a reliability lever rather than just a perk?
options: Compensation has no measurable effect on how incidents are handled
It only matters for legal compliance reasons in some countries
Paid on-call guarantees zero missed pages
Uncompensated on-call pushes engineers toward muting alerts or rushing fixes to get back to sleep, which directly affects incident quality
questions.explain: On-call pay, per-page compensation, or comp time counteracts the incentive to mute pages or rush a fix just to end the shift sooner, which is a reliability concern, not only a fairness one.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is on-call burnout considered an incident-response problem rather than purely an HR concern?
options: Burnout is unrelated to how quickly or accurately incidents get resolved
Sleep-deprived responders take measurably longer to form an accurate mental model and make worse judgment calls like when to escalate or roll back
Burnout only affects engineers' satisfaction surveys, not their on-shift performance
Burnout is resolved entirely by offering unlimited paid time off after a rotation
questions.explain: A fatigued responder is slower to diagnose correctly and more likely to apply a fix that treats a symptom instead of the cause, which shows up directly in incident outcomes, not just morale.
